mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Foreign Parent Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar in the foreign parent's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by local notary in the country of issuance; if the issuing country is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from that country's designated competent authority. If the issuing country is not a party, authenticate the notarized document at the competent foreign ministry and then legalize it at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Public Security Ministry terrorism list, plus negative press and regulatory enforcement databases. Foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and PEP family members must be identified before incorporation and subjected to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval. Ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening of the WFOE and its counterparties are required under PBOC Order No. 3 and the 2024 AML Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation - National Enterprise Name Registration and Administration System (Enterprise Name Self-Service Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters; pinyin, English, or romanized forms are not accepted as the legal registered name. The mandatory four-tier order is: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics, and legal form suffix such as 'Limited Liability Company'. A transliteration in Chinese characters is permitted in the trade-name element, while a separate non-registered English trade name may be used on export documentation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may first online amend the structure and re-file. A formal appeal may be made by submitting an administrative reconsideration application to the next higher SAMR authority within 60 days of the written rejection, or by filing an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within 6 months. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, the proposed simplified-Chinese four-tier name, trademark search and prior-right clearance evidence, and a legal memorandum demonstrating compliance with Enterprise Name Registration Measures. If the initial reservation is nearing expiry while incorporation is in progress, an extension application may be filed before the end of the 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the statutory registered address for a WFOE. Under PRC Company Law and SAMR address registration rules, the registered address must be a real, fixed commercial premises in the registered administrative district. The local tax authority will reject tax registration if the lease, property ownership certificate, or office-use certificate is missing. Banks require physical presence and landlord or utility documentation before opening RMB or foreign currency accounts. For pre-packaged hotpot soup base distribution, a virtual mailbox cannot support inventory inspection, food storage compliance, or customs export filing; therefore virtual office is rejected for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 55% to 65% risk of an unannounced physical inspection within the first six months for a newly formed WFOE in food and seasoning distribution. Checklist: (1) compliant company name plate at the registered address; (2) original lease agreement plus property ownership certificate; (3) on-site employees or a lawful office management agent; (4) storage or distribution records evidencing commercial substance; (5) board resolution appointing a local person in charge; (6) tax filing and zero-reporting justifications; (7) current UBO register and annual report availability. Municipal SAMR and tax bureaus may conduct random spot checks; any mismatch is grounds for name revocation or inclusion on the abnormal-operations list.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 5, 13, 14, 23, 42-46, 49-50; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 2, 3, 28, 31; Regulations on the Administration of Market Subject Registration (2022), Articles 9-15; Measures for the Registration of Foreign-Funded Enterprises (various effective instruments under SAMR); Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Amendment), Articles 35 and 53.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration where the WFOE is domiciled, acting through the National Enterprise Registration Service Portal and the State Council National Integrated Online Registration Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the approved Articles of Association and the Company's Pre-Approved Name Reservation Certificate, filed electronically through the SAMR integrated enterprise registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise under the Company Law, unless the industry falls within the Foreign Investment Negative List. The subscribed capital amount, contribution currency, and capital contribution time schedule must be expressly stated in the Articles of Association. There is no mandatory blocked escrow bank account; however, the legal representative and the statutory supervisor must verify actual receipt of each capital instalment, and a certified capital verification report shall be obtained when required by the settlement bank, credit grantors, or counterparties under trade finance arrangements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, at a duly convened and properly constituted first meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company Name] Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise Company Limited (the 'Company'), held at the registered office on [Date], with all directors present in person or by valid proxy and all having waived formal notice pursuant to the Articles of Association, the following resolutions were adopted on the date written above.

1. Share Capital Subscription and Verification. The Board ratified the registered capital of the Company in the amount of RMB [Amount], represented by the equity interests subscribed by the Sole Shareholder as set out in the Articles of Association. The Board approved the subscription instruments and directed that each capital instalment be remitted to the Company's capital contribution account before any business commencement. The Board instructed the General Manager to obtain from the statutory supervisor a written confirmation of receipt of each capital contribution, and, where prudentially necessary, to procure a capital verification certificate from a licensed accounting firm.

2. Banking Authorization and Signing Powers. The Board resolved to open one or more RMB and foreign currency corporate accounts with [Bank Name], and to execute all account opening agreements, SWIFT/TT instruction forms, foreign exchange purchase and settlement declarations, and letter of credit application documents. The Board authorized the Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer jointly, in any two-signature combination, to direct all payment transactions, loan documents, and trade finance instruments, with any material transaction exceeding [Amount] being further subject to a treasury resolution or board confirmation.

3. Registered Office and Physical Premises. The Board adopted the current premises located at [Full Address] as the Company's legal registered office for statutory registrations, service of process, corporate communications, and regulatory inspections. The Board directed the General Manager to execute the lease contract, file the lease authenticity confirmation, landlord consent letter, and property ownership certificate with the Market Supervision Administration, and to obtain the landlord's fire safety declaration before the premises are used for warehousing or storage of pre-packaged hotpot products.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers and Corporate Governance. The Board appointed [Name] as the sole Executive Director and Legal Representative, [Name] as the Supervisory Board's Supervisor, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Quality and Food Safety Compliance Officer. The Board confirmed that the Supervisor shall not concurrently serve as the Legal Representative or the General Manager, in accordance with the Company Law and the Articles. The Board delegated authority to the General Manager to negotiate, contract, and execute all operational agreements, employment contracts, and regulatory filings, and to use the Company seal in compliance with the Seal Management Rules adopted by this Board.

5. General Authorization and Ratification. The Board resolved that the Legal Representative and the General Manager, or their lawful delegates, are authorized to complete foreign investment information reporting, statistical declarations, tax registration with the State Taxation Administration, social insurance registration, housing fund registration, customs registration where applicable, and all other post-registration filings, and to do all acts necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Foreign-Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Platform; Ministry of Commerce foreign investment information reporting system for industry pre-clearance in restricted sectors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for the proposed WFOE, selecting a Chinese company name in the format approved under the Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration, and simultaneously verify that the stated business scope, particularly export distribution of pre-packaged hotpot soup base, does not fall within the prohibited or restricted categories of the Foreign Investment Negative List (2023 version). The application must include at least 3 alternative name candidates, the proposed business scope in both Chinese and English, and the identity and jurisdiction of each intended shareholder. Any ambiguity in the business scope wording must be resolved before filing; all descriptions must align with the ISIC 4638 wholesale distribution activity. If the applicant or a shareholder is subject to a foreign sanction or has an adverse credit record, the submission shall include an explanatory memorandum. The portal will issue a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 6 months.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Application Form (SAMR standard form)
Passport or corporate identity document of the sole shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Proposed business scope wording in English and Chinese
Foreign Investment Negative List self-assessment memorandum
3 alternative English and Chinese company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or forbidden characters, file an administrative reconsideration or an immediate amended application with a new primary name, and resubmit within 2 working days; if negative list screening identifies a restricted activity, quarantine the restricted wording from the business scope and apply for a separate sector-specific license before resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Legalization of the Sole Shareholder's Identity and Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction; Chinese Embassy/Consulate or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing country under the Hague Apostille Convention (if applicable to the shareholder's jurisdiction).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation agent shall arrange for notarization of the shareholder's certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, current registered address, and extract of directors, and for the subsequent apostille or consular legalization of these notarized documents for acceptance by Chinese market supervision authorities and the relevant bank. Each document must be translated into Chinese by a qualified translation service and the translation must include the translator's certification and company stamp. If the shareholder is a natural person, a notarized copy of the passport and a sworn declaration of lawful source of capital are required. The agent shall verify with the local SAMR office whether the scanned electronic versions of apostilled documents are acceptable for online submission; otherwise, physical copies must be delivered by courier to the registration authority. Any expiry date on the apostille or notarization should be checked against the filing timeline to avoid a gap.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of the shareholder (or notarized passport of a natural person)
Certificate of good standing issued within the last 3 months
Apostille certificate or Chinese consular legalization
Certified Chinese translation of all required documents
Sworn declaration of lawful source of capital
Power of attorney notarized and apostilled
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the consulate rejects the legalization application because of an invalid signature or seal, obtain a fresh notarization and a new apostille from the competent authority, and simultaneously request an extension of the name reservation certificate. If the translation is queried, replace the translator and provide an amended certified translation, with the correction to be received by the SAMR counter within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Establishment Registration Application through the SAMR Integrated Enterprise Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration of the city or district of the registered office, acting under SAMR; the online portal is the State Council National Integrated Online Government Service Platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation agent shall upload the completed Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company, the approved Articles of Association, the Name Reservation Certificate, the lease contract for the registered office, the landlord's property ownership certificate, the notarized and apostilled shareholder identity documents, and the credentials of the proposed legal representative, supervisor, and general manager. The application must specifically declare that the registered capital is subscribed and will be paid in accordance with a schedule contained in the Articles; if the business scope includes food wholesale and warehousing, the application must also state that the food business license will be obtained prior to actual sales. The electronic filing must be signed by the proposed legal representative using the SAMR authentication tool or a CA-certified mobile signature. After preliminary review, the local SAMR will issue a notice of acceptance or a one-time list of corrections.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Establishment Registration (SAMR FORM-1)
Notarized and apostilled shareholder documents and translations
Name Reservation Certificate
Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder and proposed legal representative
Proof of registered office address: lease agreement, landlord title certificate, and authorization letter
Passport-sized identity photographs and copies of identity documents of the legal representative, supervisor, and general manager
Consent letters signed by each proposed statutory officer
Foreign investment information reporting form
Board resolution on registered office and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for material discrepancies, the agent shall rectify the identified items within the statutory correction period of 10 working days; if the query relates to registered office ownership, a substitute notarized premises availability certificate from the local subdistrict registry may be provided; if the application is rejected, the agent shall prepare a fresh application using the corrected data and expedite by means of a priority counter submission where available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Collection of the Business License, Company Seals, and Statutory Registration Numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (license issuance) and the public security licensed seal engraving service company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the establishment application is approved, the legal representative or the authorized agent shall collect the Unified Social Credit Code certificate and the new WFOE business license at the SAMR office or download the electronic license through the official portal. The company then shall engage a public-security-licensed seal engraver to produce the company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, contract seal, and invoice seal. The seal engraver will destroy the seal, and samples and electronic images will be recorded with the public security organ. Immediately thereafter, the General Manager shall apply for the commodity code (bar code) registration with Chinese Article Numbering Association for the pre-packaged hotpot product line. The legal representative shall also initiate the customs registration for export in the cross-border trade 'single window', obtaining the customs USD code and the customs declaration system account.
required_dossiers: Original application approval notice from SAMR
Business license collection authorization letter
Legal representative identity certificate
Seal engraving application forms approved by public security
Tax, social insurance, and customs registration questionnaires
Warehouse address and lease proof for the physical business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license contains any typographical error in the business scope or registered capital, immediately apply for a correction under the SAMR correction procedure; if seal engraving is delayed by public security review, request a temporary confirmation letter from the formation agent to permit tax and bank account opening; if customs registration is blocked, file the missing documentation through the single window and request administrative reconsideration in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Foreign Exchange, Social Insurance, Food Business Licensing, and Export Regulatory Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local bureau; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) designated bank; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security; local Market Supervision Administration for food business license; General Administration of Customs through the China International Trade Single Window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The WFOE shall complete tax registration information reporting within 30 days of the business license issuance, register with the VAT taxpayer classification system, and apply for the approval to issue special VAT invoices. Simultaneously, the company shall open a RMB basic deposit account and a foreign currency settlement account with a bank designated by SAFE, and complete the foreign investment payment and receipt registration through the digital SAFE supervision platform. Social insurance and housing fund accounts shall be opened for all future employees. The food business license application shall be filed with the local SAMR food section covering wholesale and warehousing of pre-packaged foods, accompanied by a food storage environment plan, product traceability documents, and food safety responsibility statement. Finally, the customs export registration and product export filing shall be completed, including the intended customs HS codes for spicy tallow hotpot base, and a letter of credit and SWIFT payment operating procedure shall be adopted.
required_dossiers: Business license original and certified copy
Articles of Association and Minute of First Board Resolution
Bank account opening application and expected SAFE capital remittance schedule
Tax registration form and VAT questionnaire
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
Food Business License application form, premises layout, food safety management system, and staff health certificates
Customs registration application and product composition sheet for HS classification
Bank AML awareness statement for trade finance and letter of credit transactions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration reveals a mismatch in the business license data, the company shall file a one-time corrective amendment with SAMR before re-reporting to the tax bureau. If the bank refuses the corporate account due to KYC insufficiency, provide the notarized ultimate beneficial owner declaration and source-of-wealth statement. If the food business license inspection fails, the warehouse must be upgraded to meet food storage hygiene requirements and a re-inspection can be scheduled within 5 working days. If customs classification is challenged, the company shall submit a written advance ruling request to the customs tariff division, and may alternatively obtain a binding tariff information consultation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (food business licensing and food storage supervision); Ministry of Emergency Management and its local Fire and Rescue Brigade (warehouse fire permit); Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau (environmental filing); General Administration of Customs (export licensing and food export filing).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business License for the Wholesale and Storage of Pre-Packaged Food (valid for the distribution of prepackaged hotpot soup base), together with an Export Food Producer/Distributor Registration Filing under the General Administration of Customs and a Fire Safety Compliance Certificate for the storage warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE), implemented by the Municipal Bureau of Ecology and Environment at the registered warehouse location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Filing / Off-line Registration (Category 6-1 for warehouse and logistics projects under the 2021 Environmental Impact Assessment Classification List): No full EIA report is required for a non-hazardous foodstuff warehouse with no chemical processing, no combustion process, and floor area below 10,000 square meters; however, an online Environmental Impact Registration Form must be completed and publicized.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: domestic sewage from staff use and equipment cleaning must be discharged into municipal sewers under the Discharge Standard for Pollutants from Municipal Wastewater Treatment Plants (GB 18918-2002) indirect discharge requirements or local sewer quality standards, with pH 6-9, chemical oxygen demand (COD) not exceeding 500 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) not exceeding 300 mg/L, suspended solids (SS) not exceeding 400 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 45 mg/L, and oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs): because this is a non-manufacturing warehouse, no significant fugitive VOC emissions are generated; any incidental cleaning or refrigerant degassing operations must comply with the Fugitive Emission Standard for Volatile Organic Compounds (GB 37822-2019), with the emission concentration at the boundary not exceeding 40 mg/m3 for non-methane total hydrocarbons and any single VOC species not exceeding 20 mg/m3. Hazardous waste: waste oil from forklift maintenance, condensate contaminated with refrigerant, fluorescent lamps, and packaging waste contaminated with food residues must be stored in sealed containers in a dedicated waste room, labeled under the National Hazardous Waste List, transported by a licensed hazardous waste carrier, and disposed of by a permitted terminal, with on-site storage duration not exceeding one year and a waste transfer manifest retained for not less than 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate for the storage warehouse issued by the Fire and Rescue Brigade following a fire safety inspection, confirming compliance with the Fire Protection Law and the Code of Fire Protection Design for Buildings (GB 50016-2014, 2018 edition), including an automatic fire alarm and sprinkler system where warehouse floor area exceeds the prescribed threshold, two smoke-proof emergency exits, fire extinguishers at 20-meter intervals, and an annual fire safety inspection contract. In addition, a structural load inspection certificate from a licensed design institute or qualified inspection body is required to confirm that the hotpot base pallet storage racks and oil-containing product stacks are within the floor bearing capacity. Workplace safety approval under the Work Safety Law shall be evidenced by a safety management manual, a food-safety handling procedure, occupational health screening for warehouse workers, and an emergency evacuation drill record. If the premises include a cold storage annex or heated melting room for the tallow bricks, additional mechanical ventilation, floor drainage, and fire separation approvals shall be obtained from the Municipal Fire and Rescue Brigade before the relevant equipment is energized.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online portal: National Unified Electronic Taxpayer Service (e-Tax/Electronic Taxpayer Platform) accessible through provincial/municipal STA systems
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the CN_WFOE_LTD, the WFOE is the resident taxpayer. Stage 1: the foreign investors complete the Foreign Investment Information Report through the Ministry of Commerce portal, then obtain the business licence from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) with a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Stage 2: under the 'one licence, one code' reform, SAMR transmits the formation data to the STA and the tax record is automatically created; the USCC is simultaneously the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN/VAT ID), replacing any separate tax-registration certificate. Stage 3: within 30 days of issue, the WFOE's legal representative, using real-name authentication, logs into the e-Tax portal and finalises the supplementary tax record (shareholders, ultimate beneficial owner, accounting policy, bank account, and payroll/withholding profiles), which activates the taxpayer account. Stage 4: the WFOE applies for small-scale or general VAT taxpayer treatment if its annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, or elects general taxpayer status for input-VAT deduction. Stage 5: if exporting, the WFOE completes the GACC customs-registration code process and the SAFE trade-in-goods foreign-exchange registration. A non-resident foreign corporate shareholder without a PRC establishment does not obtain a Chinese TIN solely for holding the WFOE; if the WFOE pays PRC-source dividends/interest/royalties, the WFOE obtains the investor's reference code through the withholding registration function.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax legal system does not provide check-the-box, partnership passthrough, or hybrid mismatch election mechanisms for a limited-liability WFOE; the entity is always an entity-level taxable resident company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The WFOE's legal-entity tax registration is mandatory upon business licensing, with no de minimis turnover exemption. The qualifying regime threshold is RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales: once exceeded, the WFOE must be registered as a general VAT taxpayer and apply the standard 13% rate to sales of taxable goods such as pre-packaged hotpot soup base; below RMB 5,000,000 the WFOE may remain a small-scale taxpayer (current levy rate 3%, with temporary reductions) or voluntarily elect general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under the Golden Tax Project IV and the all-electronic invoice framework, the WFOE must issue compliant VAT invoices through the national e-invoice service platform. The platform validates each invoice, assigns a State-controlled invoice code/serial number, applies an encrypted anti-counterfeit stamp, and uploads the invoice data to the STA in near real time through the enterprise's tax control device (tax U-Key) or digital electronic invoice key. At issuance, all invoices (paper special/ordinary VAT invoices during the transition, and digital electronic invoices in pilot areas) are transmitted to the tax authority's clearance nodes. The WFOE must report issued invoices on the monthly e-filing, reconcile delivered/issued invoice data, obtain electronic approval for red-letter credit notes, and, if using enterprise ERP/billing systems, connect to the official e-invoice API where required by provincial tax authorities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The WFOE general VAT taxpayer may claim the PRC zero export VAT rate on the pre-packaged hotpot soup base only where the goods are declared to and released by GACC for physical export outside the customs territory, sold by and invoiced in the name of the WFOE to an overseas buyer, and the export proceeds are received in foreign currency through the designated banking system. If the goods are supplied to a foreign party without actual customs exportation, no zero-rating/refund applies. Qualifying offshore services/digital supplies remain subject to the statutory cross-border VAT zero-rating catalogue and require documentary proof of performance outside China for a non-resident customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Cargo Export Declaration) with GACC release/clearance result code
Commercial invoice issued by the WFOE
Bill of Lading (B/L) or equivalent air waybill/combined transport document
Export sales contract and purchase order
Bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher (bank settlement memo, SWIFT credit advice, or equivalent inward remittance certificate) evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Export VAT rebate/exemption declaration form submitted through the e-Tax platform when refund is claimed
SAFE foreign-exchange monitoring records reconciling goods description, customs date, invoice amount, and payment receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, GACC, and SAFE jointly cross-check customs declaration data, e-invoice records, transport documents, and bank receipts. Where zero-rating or export VAT refund is claimed on goods not actually exported, with misrepresented or false customs declarations, without genuine foreign-exchange repatriation, or beyond the 180-day repatriation deadline unless an approved extension exists, the tax authority will reverse the zero-rating, claw back all VAT refunds paid, impose daily late-payment surcharges of 0.05% of the unpaid tax, and levy penalties of 0.5 to 5 times the evaded tax under the Law on Tax Collection and Administration. Intentional fraudulent export refunds will also be transferred for criminal investigation under the Criminal Law's false-export tax-refund offence, punishable by fines, confiscation, and imprisonment up to life imprisonment; the WFOE's export tax-rebate status and Customs credit rating may be suspended or downgraded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with strict current account convertibility but significant capital account controls. The RMB is convertible for trade in goods and services, and foreign exchange received from export proceeds may be retained or settled under SAFE's Qualified Foreign Exchange Settlement system, but the balance must be declared and reconciled through the Foreign Exchange Administration Platform. Profit remittance by a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) requires audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and proof of capital verification through the SAFE registration system. While current account items such as trade payments and dividends from lawful profits are generally permitted, capital account items such as foreign debt injection or equity capital increases require separate SAFE registration and may face waiting periods or quota limits. The WFOE must convert registered paid-in capital into RMB at a domestic bank through the capital account system, and outbound remittances of funds not representing true trade or lawfully declared dividends will be blocked. Surrender of export proceeds is no longer mandatory under the 2019 SAFE reforms; exporters may retain foreign currency in licensed bank accounts or settle on a voluntary basis, but all receipts above USD 500,000 must be electronically reported within 30 days through the SAFE digital platform. In practice, banks apply post-verification systems, and any mismatch between customs declarations, invoices, and logistics documents will trigger a foreign exchange adjudication review. The Central Bank implements macro-prudential cross-border financing parameters for WFOEs, including the discretion to adjust upper limits on net assets and to enforce counter-cyclical factors, meaning external borrowing by the WFOE must pass a Foreign Debt Macro-Prudential Regulation registration before funds can be brought onshore. The de facto non-convertibility of the capital account and the paper-intensive nature of dividend repatriation require treasury teams to maintain documentary discipline across every inbound and outbound payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since the SAFE Circular 28 Fa (2019) reform, there is no mandatory conversion ratio or statutory surrender timeline for current-account export receipts. Exporters may retain FX proceeds in a domestic foreign currency account or voluntarily settle into RMB; however, all export-related FX receipts must be reported to SAFE through the bank within 30 days of receipt using bank transaction reporting codes 101010 (export trade in goods). Receipts above USD 500,000, and all receipts from sensitive jurisdictions, require supporting customs declaration records, commercial invoices, bills of lading, and sales contracts. The bank must verify that the receiving entity is the actual exporter under the customs registration number. If the WFOE receives payment into an offshore account instead of repatriating, the transaction must be disclosed under the offshore retained proceeds filing requirement, and the retained amount may trigger capital verification adjustments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account, Operating RMB Account and Export Proceeds USD Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic RMB Settlement Account and Safe-Deposit FX Current Account
Capital Injection Account and Trade Settlement Account
RMB Operations Account and Export Receivables USD Collection Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium (if the branch has established cross-border team support)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking rail. The PRC regulators require full bank account opening through a licensed domestic bank branch, and the WFOE must have a physical registered business address and a Chinese business license. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Payoneer, or Currenxie cannot be used as the principal settlement channel because the SAFE system and People's Bank of China settlement platforms require domestic bank participation for capital injection, customs reconciliation, export proceeds verification, and tax refund matching. Foreign EMIs may only serve as auxiliary collection tools for certain cross-border e-commerce receivables, but even then the funds must be routed back to a domestic bank account and declared under the cross-border e-commerce revenue code. For this entity, which is exporting pre-packaged hotpot soup base prepared for bulk wholesale, the corporate treasury must rely on state-owned banks to obtain the necessary SAFE registration, customs linkage, and licensing verification. No fintech EMI can provide a compliant capital verification report or meet the Foreign Investment Disbursement-related documentation requirements of SAFE.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory for the statutory legal representative and at least one second director or shareholder representative during the initial account activation of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise. The bank compliance officer will conduct an on-site interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for the primary operating bank account. Where the legal representative is a non-resident foreign national, in-branch identity verification must be supported by a valid passport entry stamp, visa, or residence permit, and if the legal representative is outside China, a notarized and China-consulate-authenticated power of attorney may allow the Finance Manager or another named director to appear in branch, but the legal representative must still complete a video-based KYC session recorded by the bank. In practice, tier-1 state-owned banks require the company chop (official seal), the financial seal, the legal representative seal, and the original business license to be presented physically. Any deviation requires a head-office exception approval and significantly downgrades onboarding viability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by the layered WFOE holding structure with offshore shareholders, especially when the ultimate shareholder is not the named bank signatory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A corporate ownership chart down to the ultimate natural person, certified by a Singapore or Hong Kong registered agent, a notarized certificate of incumbency from each intermediate holding company, board resolutions authorising the WFOE account signatories, full incorporation registry extracts for each layer, and a pledge of the ultimate natural person's passport copy, proof of residence, and source-of-wealth summary for each controller holding above 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Biodiesel or food-industry licensing risk because the entity is registered under pre-packaged hotpot soup base distribution, which triggers customs food import/export registration and pre-package label compliance checks by AQSIQ/GACC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Chinese Food Business License (food production or food operation license), GACC food export enterprise registration filing, ISO 22000 or HACCP certification if available, product hazard analysis summary, pre-package label compliance declarations for export markets, and a certificate of sanitary inspection for each batch from the customs authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering suspicion from wide variance between the declared customs value of the hotpot base bricks and the invoice unit price, or from mismatched HS codes and commodity descriptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales contracts, purchase orders, proforma invoices, commodity HS code classification memo, independent unaffiliated laboratory analysis report confirming the product composition (tallow, chili, base paste, spices), customs declaration records for previous export tranches, and a logistics custody trail showing warehouse receipts, transport bills, and quality inspection certificates with sealed Chinese customs stamps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments from unconnected third-party collection accounts or from individuals instead of the named foreign buyer's corporate bank account, which would trigger automatic AML screening by the bank compliance module.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A declared list of counterparties from the parent wholesale transaction records, a PDF customer onboarding form naming each foreign buyer's registered office and bank relationship manager, bank statements of the pilot export transaction showing the actual remitter and beneficiary, an explanation of the commercial invoice/receivables assignment if any account receivable monetisation is used, and an undertaking that all future remittances will originate solely from the buyer's corporate account as listed in the KYC inventory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the WFOE equity capital injection, the offshore parent must wire USD or RMB via SWIFT MT103 into the bank branch named in the Foreign-Invested Enterprise registration, using SAFE payment purpose code 620141 for capital injection. Before execution, the WFOE must complete Foreign Investment (FDI) information reporting through the SAFE digital platform or the domestic bank's foreign exchange business system, and the bank will verify the corporate name, registration certificate (currently integrated with business license), and the equity subscription clause in the articles of association. The remitting shareholder's bank name and SWIFT BIC must correspond with the registered shareholder. After the funds arrive at the bank's capital settlement account, the WFOE must apply for conversion into RMB using the Foreign Currency Purchase / Capital Settlement form, after which the bank transfers RMB to the designated basic deposit account. The capital verification must be performed by a licensed Chinese certified public accountant (CPA) who issues a capital verification report in Chinese. The WFOE must then file the capital verification report with the local Administration for Market Regulation. Any transfer of the converted RMB from the operating account to third-party vendors must be supported by invoices, contracts, payroll records, service agreements, or lease contracts to survive SAFE post-verification scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The preferred rail is a banker's acceptance or a direct SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlement with verified buyers in Singapore, Hong Kong, and mainland China's free-trade zones. For sales to buyers in Western markets that require transport documentary protection, Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight) are recommended with the negotiating bank being the same tier-1 domestic bank, and the advising bank should be a major regional clearing bank in the importer's country. Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) are a viable secondary rail for established buyers but carry a higher receivable risk. All trade disbursements must be paid from the operating RMB account through the cross-border RMB settlement system (CIPS) or via the domestic bank's SWIFT network after submitting the e-tax clearance, customs export declaration, and transaction matching. Outbound payments to pay for cow tallow, spices, packaging, and labour must use RMB/CNY participation in CIPS if possible, or SWIFT MT103 with trade purpose codes under current account items. Any outbound rail involving an offshore intermediate PSP or factoring house must be taged with a full assignment agreement and must still be receivable in the WFOE's own bank account before goods departure, unless the bank grants warehouse financing and LC negotiation facilities separately.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Bank-intermediated RMB/USD spot conversion for immediate settlement of approved current account trades

Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards with a tenors of up to 12 months for RMB against USD, EUR, or HKD, where the underlying is a verified trade invoice, a purchase order, or a cash-flow forecast submitted to the domestic bank; the forward must be concluded with a licensed onshore bank and must not require an offshore NDF counterparty unless the bank uses the SAFE interbank market via the onshore CNY fixing

Foreign exchange swaps between USD and RMB for up to one year to manage working capital cash-flow mismatches among collection of export proceeds, payment of tallow import costs, and dividend repatriation date, provided the swap is documented against actual receivables/payables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore; the WFOE must use deliverable forwards onshore or, if entering an offshore NDF through its parent, the underlying must be the parent's own offshore treasury, and the settlement difference must not be repatriated into the WFOE as income without proper trade documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report including Foreign Investment Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, jointly with Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign investment data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June following the close of the previous calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the deadline results in inclusion on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations. If the omission is not remedied within three consecutive years, the company is placed on the List of Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprises, triggering joint disciplinary measures, credit restrictions, banking and customs constraints, and potential administrative revocation of the business licence by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the national information publicity system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June; any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding transfer must be reported within 30 calendar days from the date of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Beneficial Ownership Information Administration Measures (effective 1 March 2024), a warning and corrective order are issued first; persistent non-compliance may attract an administrative fine of up to RMB 50,000 for the enterprise and up to RMB 10,000 for the directly responsible officer. Repeated violations can lead to inclusion in the dishonest enterprise list and administrative strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Customs Enterprise Report for registered import/export food trader
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (GACC) via the customs enterprise credit platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June in respect of the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the customs annual report is not filed, customs registration is placed on hold and export declaration privileges are immediately suspended. If the omission persists for 12 months, the customs registration is annulled, resulting in irreversible loss of export clearance capacity and qualification as a compliant trader, which may be treated as a statutory strike-off event.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement (Enterprise Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May following the close of the tax year (calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest accrues at 0.05% per day on any underpaid corporate income tax from the statutory payment deadline. Administrative fines for failure to file or inaccurate filing range up to RMB 2,000 for slight cases and up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases, together with mandatory enforced collection and potential restriction of export tax rebates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOEs) in China are subject to a categorical annual statutory audit requirement, irrespective of any numeric size exemption. This obligation is rooted in the historical foreign-invested enterprise audit rules and continues to be applied through the annual reporting requirements administered by SAMR and the tax administration for foreign-funded companies. In addition, for a wholesale enterprise classified under ISIC 4638 / NAICS 424490, local SAMR and tax authorities typically impose an independent certified CPA audit when any of the following quantitative triggers is exceeded: (a) year-end total assets exceed RMB 50 million; (b) annual operating revenue exceeds RMB 50 million; or (c) average employee headcount exceeds 100. Export-oriented WFOEs may also be required to produce an audited financial statement to substantiate VAT export refund claims, even if the company is below the revenue or asset thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: People's Republic of China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / Chinese GAAP) issued by the Ministry of Finance. IFRS is not directly applicable for statutory regulatory filings; however, if the WFOE is a consolidated subsidiary of an overseas parent, group reporting may require IFRS reconciliation. A small or micro enterprise may prepare its statements under the Small Business Accounting Standards (SBAS), but the annual audit obligation for a foreign-invested entity still requires the report to be prepared in accordance with ASBE and accompanied by a Chinese certified public accountant's audit opinion.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Beneficial Ownership Information Administration Measures (PBOC and SAMR Order, effective 1 March 2024), the WFOE must identify and record all ultimate beneficial owners in a dedicated register, and report the required information to SAMR. On every annual filing cycle, the company must log into the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System before 30 June and confirm that the previously disclosed beneficial ownership data remain accurate. Any change in the beneficial ownership structure, including a shareholding transfer that alters control or ownership rights, must be reported within 30 calendar days from the date of the transfer or amendment. Failure to update the register and report the change in time subjects the company to administrative warning, corrective orders, and the monetary penalties described in the annual compliance calendar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$700 – US$1,800 per year for a registered office or corporate service agent in tier-1 Chinese cities such as Shanghai, Beijing, or Guangzhou
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500 – US$5,000 per year depending on revenue, asset size, number of subsidiaries, and complexity of export transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China applies a 25% headline Enterprise Income Tax rate to resident companies such as a PRC Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise; available effective-rate relief includes the Small Low-Profit Enterprise regime which applies a 20% reduced rate with a current grace-period effective preferential rate of 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3,000,000 where all statutory conditions are met, the 15% preferential rate for qualified High and New Technology Enterprises, the 15% Western Region encouraged-industry rate, a 100% additional R&D super-deduction for qualifying proprietary hotpot soup base food-science development, and a special reinvestment deferral allowing the 10% dividend withholding tax to be postponed if distributable profits are reinvested in encouraged China sectors; there is no general free-zone CIT exemption or patent box for food distribution activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: China State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau; Form A100000 Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Class A) together with the complete A-Class supporting schedules including A105000 tax reconciliation, A105080 depreciation, A107010/A107012 preferential and R&D super-deduction schedules, A108000 foreign tax credit schedule, and the integrated Annual Related Party Transaction Reporting Table
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement plus quarterly provisional CIT prepayments; quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end and the final annual reconciliation return is due by 31 May following the tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year WFOE: each quarterly provisional CIT prepayment is due by 15 April, 15 July, 15 October and 15 January; the annual return and any balancing tax payment must be filed and paid by 31 May of the following calendar year; a fiscal-year entity following a non-calendar accounting period is required to file by the fifth month after the close of that fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all export turnover from pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base, converted from foreign currency at the STA monthly central parity rate and reconciled to customs export declarations, letters of credit and Swift TT receipts. The Chinese resident WFOE must not net intra-group recharges that strip distribution margin offshore; if a non-resident shareholder controls sales and inventory risk, the reported revenue and transfer pricing adjustment will be challenged, and the annual return must reflect arm's-length gross profit.

Report cost of goods sold consisting of raw food materials, packaging, subcontract production and direct labor, but only where the WFOE has legal title, inventory risk and physical flow through China. A paper WFOE that merely passes purchase orders to an offshore affiliate and holds no economic substance may be denied these deductions and have profit reallocated to the foreign shareholder.

Include urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, property tax, land-use tax, stamp duty and other deductible business taxes. VAT itself is excluded from the CIT base, and any erroneously claimed VAT export refund must not be booked as a cost; intentional refund overstatements expose directors to criminal false-export invoice exposure.

Disclose freight, port charges, logistics, overseas warehousing, platform commissions and trade promotion expenses. Deductions require compliant original invoices or equivalent evidence; payments to a Hong Kong or offshore related-party logistic provider must satisfy the CUPreasonable services test, demonstrate actual receipt of services, and be covered by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

Include director salaries, office rent, professional fees, insurance and information technology costs; entertainment is deductible only up to 60% of expenditures and capped at 0.5% of operating revenue, and personal expenses of non-resident shareholders are non-deductible and may be recharacterized as deemed dividends subject to withholding tax.

Interest on related-party borrowings is deductible only up to the arm's-length rate and within the statutory debt-to-equity thin capitalization limits of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises and 5:1 for financial enterprises. Excess interest is permanently non-deductible and remains subject to 10% statutory withholding tax when paid to a non-resident lender absent a treaty reduction.

Cash dividends received by the WFOE from a mainland-resident subsidiary are generally exempt from CIT under Article 26, but equity disposal gains are taxable. Dividends declared by the WFOE to its foreign parent are not deducted in this return; they are after-tax distributions subject to separate dividend withholding tax, not CIT deductions.

Enter the accounting profit before tax prepared under PRC Accounting Standards; the WFOE then effects the tax reconciliation through Schedule A105000. The accounting profit must be internally consistent with audited financial statements, export VAT refund schedules, and the annual related-party transaction table; inconsistency is an immediate audit trigger.

Add back non-deductible entertainment disallowance, excessive related-party interest, inflated non-resident service fees, unsupported impairment provisions, non-compliant invoices, and any voluntary transfer pricing adjustment. Cross-border transactions with zero substance or no commercial justification should be adjusted here to avoid GAAR recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment deductions and tax-exempt income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct qualifying R&D super-deduction, tax-exempt interest and resident-subsidiary dividends, and eligible government grants. Treaty exemptions do not reduce the WFOE's taxable income; a bilateral tax treaty only affects withholding tax on payments made by the WFOE to its non-resident shareholder.

Offset prior-year tax losses that were established with proper documentation and remain within the ordinary 5-year carryforward window; high-technology and small low-profit enterprises may enjoy longer statutory carryforward periods where eligible. A China exporter that consistently reports losses on large related-party overseas sales while the foreign parent earns profits will have those losses disregarded and reallocated under arm's-length principles.

The resulting taxable income must reflect an arm's-length reward for the WFOE's procurement, distribution, inventory, credit and logistics functions; if the profit margin on pre-packaged hotpot soup base export sales is materially below the interquartile range of Chinese comparable wholesalers, the STA may impose a special tax adjustment under Article 41.

Apply the 25% statutory rate; a qualified High and New Technology Enterprise or Western Region encouraged enterprise may use 15%, and a qualified small low-profit enterprise uses the reduced 20% regime with the current preferential calculation producing an effective 5% rate on taxable income up to RMB 3,000,000. Preferential rates must be self-assessed and documented, not assumed based on the foreign shareholding structure.

Credit foreign income tax only for creditable foreign-source income actually included in the Chinese tax base and only within the per-item Chinese tax limitation; transfer pricing adjustments triggered by a foreign PE require Schedule A108000 and cannot create a second offshore offset for the same profit distribution.

The annual CIT amount less total quarterly provisional prepayments must be settled by 31 May; an unpaid balance cannot be discharged by a corresponding dividend withholding obligation because the CIT liability is that of the resident WFOE while the withholding obligation arises separately on the remittance of dividends to the non-resident parent.

Complete the integrated annual related-party transaction information in the E-Tax system, disclosing every controlled transaction with the foreign shareholder, affiliated distributors, IP licensors and financing parties; provide transaction amount, jurisdiction, pricing method and beneficial-ownership status. Willful omission of a substantial cross-border related-party transaction is treated as false declaration and can be prosecuted as tax fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increasing to RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 for serious cases under Articles 62 of the Law on Tax Administration and Collection; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax under Article 32; under-payment by false declaration or concealment attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63; failure to report related-party transactions or to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation may trigger a penalty of RMB 10,000 as well as the special tax adjustment interest of the PBOC benchmark rate plus five percentage points; instances of intentional tax evasion exceeding the criminal threshold of RMB 50,000 and 10% of taxable tax expose responsible directors to criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on outbound dividends paid by the Chinese resident WFOE to its non-resident corporate shareholder under CIT Law Articles 3 and 37; the rate can be reduced to 5% under a qualifying double tax treaty when the beneficial owner is a company resident in the treaty jurisdiction and directly holds at least 25% of the paying company's capital throughout the applicable 365-day period, and other DTAs may provide 0% or reduced rates depending on shareholding and holding period; a non-resident individual shareholder usually faces 20% dividend withholding unless the treaty prescribes a lower rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting a dividend, the WFOE as withholding agent must obtain from the foreign shareholder a current-year Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a signed beneficial-ownership declaration confirming that the shareholder is not a nominee, agent or flow-through entity, and share registers and board resolutions evidencing the required direct holding and holding period. The withholding agent must then file the reduced-rate withholding through the China Electronic Tax Bureau under the SAT Bulletin 2019 No. 35 mechanism for non-resident taxpayers enjoying treaty benefits, retaining all supporting documents for at least 10 years. If the foreign shareholder has no economic substance and no core income-generating activities, the tax authority will deny DTA relief, require the 10% statutory withholding to be paid, impose late-payment surcharge and penalties, and may classify the arrangement as treaty abuse under GAAR.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: China's statutory withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties to a non-resident beneficial owner is 10% of the gross amount under CIT Law Articles 3 and 37; bilateral double tax treaties may reduce interest and royalty withholding, for example to 7% interest and 7% royalties under the China-Hong Kong DTA, to 7% under certain other DTA protocols, or to 5-10% depending on the IP type and ownership, but the reduced rate is conditioned on Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership, no attributable Chinese permanent establishment, and compliance with any limitation-on-benefits clause. The same thin-capitalization ceiling applies to related-party interest, and royalty payments to an offshore affiliate are scrutinized for surplus gratuitous transfer, valuation and source-site substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The WFOE must prepare contemporaneous Local File documentation when the prior-year related-party transaction amount exceeds: RMB 200,000,000 for tangible goods, RMB 100,000,000 for intangible property transfers or usage, RMB 100,000,000 for financial asset transfers, and RMB 40,000,000 for related-party service receipts or provision; a Chinese Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least RMB 5,500,000,000 in the relevant fiscal year, and an annual related-party transaction report must be filed with the CIT annual return even below those thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not maintain a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the economic substance doctrine is applied through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under CIT Law Article 47, the beneficial-ownership test for treaty relief, the BEPS-aligned functional and risk analysis, and the judicial substance-over-form principle. The WFOE must demonstrate employees, physical premises, procurement authority, inventory risk, credit risk and management decisions in China; if the wholly foreign-owned enterprise is a non-substantive conduit through which hotpot soup base export profits are routed offshore, the STA may reallocate the profit to the value-creation jurisdiction, disallow treaty benefits and impose special-tax-adjustment interest. In addition, China's controlled foreign corporation rules apply to low-taxed offshore subsidiaries that accumulate passive income without real economic substance, requiring current-year attribution of distributable income to the Chinese investor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-border transfer pricing manipulation and profit stripping through an offshore distributor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base to a related Hong Kong or tax-haven distributor at an artificially low transfer price, creates a persistent Chinese taxable loss, removes economic substance from China, and provides no contemporaneous transfer pricing file or functional-risk analysis to justify the margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The State Taxation Administration may re-determine taxable income under CIT Law Articles 41 and 48, impose special tax adjustment interest at the benchmark lending rate plus five percentage points under the Implementing Regulations, impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 64 of the Law on Tax Administration and Collection, and extend the assessment period to 10 years for non-disclosed related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false related-party disclosures or directs the transfer-pricing manipulation can be pierced through under PRC Company Law where the corporate form is abused to harm the State's tax claim; the director may be jointly and severally liable to restore the underpaid tax, placed on the serious tax non-compliant list, subjected to exit control and travel bans, and criminally convicted for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to three years where evasion exceeds RMB 50,000 and ten percent of disclosed tax and up to seven years in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent VAT export refund through false export declarations and false special fapiao
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE or its directors fabricate overseas purchase orders, use circular Swift TT and letter of credit payments from a related nominee buyer, over-invoice or over-declare the export quantity of hotpot soup base, and claim VAT export refunds for goods not actually shipped or not qualifying for refund treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority claws back the refunded VAT, imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the fraudulently obtained refund under Law on Tax Administration and Collection Article 63, cancels export tax refund qualifications and customs registration, and refers the case to criminal authorities. Under Criminal Law Article 205, issuing false special VAT fapiao or using false fapiao to deceitfully obtain export tax refunds is punishable by custodial sentences of up to life imprisonment and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, financial controller and responsible directors are treated as directly responsible persons under Criminal Law Articles 205 and 211; they face criminal imprisonment, personal fines and confiscation of property. They are also exposed to exit bans and blacklisting by tax and customs authorities, deprivation from serving as directors or legal representatives of new companies, and civil restitution claims by the State for the fraudulent refund amount; the corporate veil will be pierced where the directors diverted refund money for personal use.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty abuse, shell shareholding and false beneficial ownership by a zero-substance nominee
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The shareholding layer above the WFOE is a Hong Kong or offshore shell company with no physical office, employees, bank account, or real decision-making capacity; the shell nominally holds a 25% or greater stake in the WFOE for 365 days in order to apply a 5% dividend treaty rate while the ultimate beneficial owner resides in a non-treaty jurisdiction, thereby avoiding China's 10% statutory dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will deny the treaty benefit and require payment of the full 10% statutory withholding tax on all dividend distributions, together with late-payment surcharge and interest; the withholding agent that failed to withhold is liable for a fine of 50% to 300% of the amount not withheld under Article 69 of the Law on Tax Administration and Collection; the offshore structure may also be recharacterized under CIT Law Article 47 as an arrangement lacking reasonable commercial purpose, subjecting the WFOE to additional tax on the deemed reallocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs a false beneficial-ownership declaration or knowingly causes the WFOE to remit dividends through a paper shell can be personally jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax under the corporate veil-piercing doctrine; the director may be blacklisted as a major tax non-compliant responsible person, banned from overseas travel, prohibited from assuming new legal representative roles, and prosecuted criminally for tax evasion where the avoided withholding exceeds the criminal threshold, with the court empowered to impose imprisonment and restitution out of personal assets.
